messages:
Ellen: FYI sampleapp typing job failed after the autogen change that started using `Final` on model constants and emitting broader union types for enums. pyright is complaining in a couple of client call sites.
Ravi: paste the pyright error?
Ellen: gist:
```
src/clients/orders_client.py:142:22 - error: Cannot assign to a final attribute "status" (reportGeneralTypeIssues)
  142 │         order.status = OrderStatus.ACTIVE
        ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
```
Ellen: We added `Final` to generated enum defaults and some consts to signal immutability, but that leaks to users who mutate model instances in-place (legacy pattern).
Sofia: Hmm. Two orthogonal issues: 1) `Final` on generated attributes is a DX regression for callers who expect mutable Pydantic models; 2) the enum union change (Enum | str) means callers that do `order.status.name` get mypy/pyright attr errors when status is str.
Ravi: For the `Final` problem, easiest fix is remove `Final` from runtime generated models. If we want to keep immutability signal for type-checkers, we can emit it in the .pyi stubs only. That way runtime remains flexible but types can be stricter for new code.
Maya: I like the stub route. We can: keep runtime files unchanged (no Final), emit deterministic .pyi alongside models introducing `Final` annotations and typed accessors, and include a `# see also: status_as_enum()` comment in the runtime file pointing to the stub accessor.
Ellen: For the enum attr issue, two patterns: accessor method (`status_as_enum`) returning Optional[OrderStatus] or property in .pyi. Stubs feel less disruptive.
Sofia: Another idea: generate a lightweight Protocol for client interfaces we expect customers to type against. That reduces surface area of type churn when models evolve. Eg:
```
class OrdersClientProtocol(Protocol):
    async def get_order(self, id: str) -> Order: ...
```
Consumers can type their functions against the Protocol, and we can evolve generated models with fewer breaking typing changes.
Ravi: Good forward-thinking. For now let's fix the immediate CI break: revert `Final` in generator, emit .pyi with `Final` where appropriate, and change enum typing to `Optional[Union[OrderStatus, str]]` + `status_as_enum` accessor in runtime. Add typing tests covering mutation and `status.name` access patterns.
CI-bot: sampleapp/typing-check failed on branch typing-final-enum-2002002002  https://ci.internal/runs/9999  logs attached.
Maya: I'll open a small PR implementing the generator change and a packaging tweak to include .pyi files in distributions. Also adding a Protocol template and sample-app typing tests.
Ellen: Please call out pyright and mypy in the PR description and note why stubs are used for stricter annotations. Some customers expect stricter types but we shouldn't break existing runtime behavior.
Ravi: Also add a smoke run job in CI that runs a cross-repo typing suite against quickstart and playground before merging.
Maya: Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autogen/pull/4810  includes: remove Final from runtime, emit .pyi with Final, enum union + accessor, OrdersClientProtocol, tests, packaging.
CI-bot: PR 4810 CI: mypy+pyright checks in sample-app passed, packaging tests passed. Merged into main at 2002002060.
Sofia: Nice compromise. This gives stricter typing opt-in via stubs/protocols while keeping runtime ergonomic. Marking resolved on my side. :white_check_mark:
